title: fix: move Qwen3 Coder 30B to AWS Bedrock
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Moves Qwen3 Coder 30B from OVHcloud to direct AWS Bedrock in us-east-1 (`qwen.qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-v1:0`). Public ID and aliases stay unchanged.
- Uses AWS standard on-demand prices: $0.15 input / $0.60 output per million tokens, multiplier 1, Paid Pollen only. [Official AWS pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/).
- Removes the unused OVH route and injected coding prompt; updates catalog parameters and the price snapshot. No fallback; the maintainer chose direct Bedrock after evaluating SiliconFlow.
- Removes this model's `/v1/responses`, seed, logprobs, and stop support. Named `tool_choice` behaves as `auto`; strict JSON schemas are not enforced through the current gateway. Prompted JSON and automatic/required tools work.
- Verified authenticated local gateway against real Bedrock: all aliases, chat/text/Messages endpoints, streaming with terminal usage, tool round trips, JSON, permissions, paid access, cache reuse, error responses, a 234K-token prompt, and a 25-request burst (25/25). Staging Tinybird usage/rates reconcile with wallet debits; cached retries do not bill again. No missing conversion warnings.

Validation: 184 related Gen tests plus focused fallback integration checks, Enter price snapshot, both service type checks, and Biome pass. Production verification follows deployment. Dashboard announcement: #16336.

gist.headline: Qwen changes flight paths
gist.blurb: Qwen3 Coder 30B takes a more direct route through AWS Bedrock. Its familiar aliases stay put; the route behind them changes.
gist.summary: Qwen3 Coder 30B moves from OVHcloud to direct AWS Bedrock in us-east-1, keeping its public ID and aliases while using Paid Pollen pricing of $0.15 input and $0.60 output per million tokens.
gist.impact: Paid Pollen requests keep the same aliases for chat, text, Messages, and streaming, but this Bedrock route does not support /v1/responses, seed, logprobs, or stop.
